t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section as a flat straight-on UI mockup in Swiss International Typographic Style on a warm limestone page. A large light-weight sans headline and a small mono breadcrumb top-left. Below, small column headers over a steel-blue hairline, then rows of a three-column table for <CONTENT>, each row led by a deep navy square tile holding a huge light off-white numeral with a slash. One tile is limestone with a faint steel-blue blueprint drawing behind its numeral. Large sans cell headings with small notes beneath. Flat, square corners.
signature_idea: Each feed-water condition gets a navy square tile with a huge slash numeral, turning a cause-effect table into a Swiss poster grid.
strengths: navy numeral tiles give strong, scannable row anchors
condition, effect, response columns are a clear reading pattern
light numerals, navy and limestone with one steel-blue accent are on-brand
the blueprint tile adds a quiet visual break
maps cleanly to a token-only CSS grid
weaknesses: dense: five rows of large cell text fill the frame with little space
blueprint in tile 03 is faint and overlaps the numeral, reading as a glitch
cell headings are large regular sans that feel heavy beside light numerals
invented temperatures and conditions would be mistaken for facts
brand_fit_why: Navy tiles, light slash numerals, limestone page and steel-blue rule fit the brand, but density and heavy cell type cost calm.
